text: Near Quảng Yên, in northern Vietnam, people digging fields and fishponds have struck something strange: large wooden stakes, buried deep in the mud.
say: Near Kwahng Yen, in northern Vietnam, people digging fields and fishponds have struck something strange: large wooden stakes, buried deep in the mud.

text: The Bạch Đằng River is a short distance away. Radiocarbon tests on samples from some of the stakes point to around the thirteenth century.
say: The Bahk Dahng River is a short distance away. Radiocarbon tests on samples from some of the stakes point to around the thirteenth century.

text: But a date for the wood is not yet a story. To connect these stakes to a battle, archaeologists had to read them alongside the written records.
say: But a date for the wood is not yet a story. To connect these stakes to a battle, archaeologists had to read them alongside the written records.

text: Those records tell of 1288, when a river and a tide helped Đại Việt destroy the fleet of Kublai Khan. And then the winner did something surprising. It sent tribute to the side it had beaten.
say: Those records tell of twelve eighty-eight, when a river and a tide helped Dye Vee-et destroy the fleet of Kublai Khan. And then the winner did something surprising. It sent tribute to the side it had beaten.

text: So this story has two puzzles. How did the trap work? And why did victory still end in tribute?
say: So this story has two puzzles. How did the trap work? And why did victory still end in tribute?

text: By the 1280s, Kublai Khan ruled China as emperor of the Yuan dynasty.
say: By the twelve-eighties, Kublai Khan ruled China as emperor of the Yuan dynasty.

text: Đại Việt, the Vietnamese kingdom ruled by the Trần family, already sent envoys and tribute. Kublai wanted more. He demanded that the Trần king come to his court in person.
say: Dye Vee-et, the Vietnamese kingdom ruled by the Chun family, already sent envoys and tribute. Kublai wanted more. He demanded that the Chun king come to his court in person.

text: The Trần kings sent envoys and gifts. They never went themselves. In the Yuan view, that was defiance.
say: The Chun kings sent envoys and gifts. They never went themselves. In the Yuan view, that was defiance.

text: In 1286, Kublai went further. He named Trần Ích Tắc, a Trần prince who had gone over to the Yuan, as king of Đại Việt, and prepared an army to put him on the throne.
say: In twelve eighty-six, Kublai went further. He named Chun Ick Tuck, a Chun prince who had gone over to the Yuan, as king of Dye Vee-et, and prepared an army to put him on the throne.

text: This was not the first Mongol army in Vietnam. In 1258, a Mongol force coming from Yunnan won a battle and took the capital, Thăng Long. It did not stay. That campaign was part of the Mongols' larger war against Song China.
say: This was not the first Mongol army in Vietnam. In twelve fifty-eight, a Mongol force coming from Yoon-nahn won a battle and took the capital, Tahng Long. It did not stay. That campaign was part of the Mongols' larger war against Song China.

text: In 1285, a much larger Yuan invasion came. Kublai's son Toghan led the army in the north, and General Sogetu advanced from Champa in the south.
say: In twelve eighty-five, a much larger Yuan invasion came. Kublai's son Toh-gahn led the army in the north, and General Soh-geh-too advanced from Chahm-pah in the south.

text: How large was it? Nobody knows. Figures in the sources range from tens of thousands to half a million, and none of them can be checked.
say: How large was it? Nobody knows. Figures in the sources range from tens of thousands to half a million, and none of them can be checked.

text: The Trần court left the capital. The Yuan occupied empty palaces. Then came the counterattack. Sogetu was killed, and Toghan pulled back to the north.
say: The Chun court left the capital. The Yuan occupied empty palaces. Then came the counterattack. Soh-geh-too was killed, and Toh-gahn pulled back to the north.

text: Both times, taking the capital did not mean taking the kingdom. The court could move, and the war went on.
say: Both times, taking the capital did not mean taking the kingdom. The court could move, and the war went on.

text: Kublai did not accept defeat. According to historians, he even set aside plans for another invasion of Japan to concentrate on the south.
say: Kublai did not accept defeat. According to historians, he even set aside plans for another invasion of Japan to concentrate on the south.

text: In late 1287, the Yuan invaded again, from two directions: armies by land from the north, and a fleet along the coast.
say: In late twelve eighty-seven, the Yuan invaded again, from two directions: armies by land from the north, and a fleet along the coast.

text: By early 1288, they held Thăng Long for the third time. And for the third time, they found a capital without a court.
say: By early twelve eighty-eight, they held Tahng Long for the third time. And for the third time, they found a capital without a court.

text: An army that far from home has to eat. The Yuan plan relied on grain ships coming by sea.
say: An army that far from home has to eat. The Yuan plan relied on grain ships coming by sea.

text: That grain fleet never arrived as planned. Vietnamese forces attacked it, and the grain was lost. Even the accounts of this disagree on where, when, and who led the attack.
say: That grain fleet never arrived as planned. Vietnamese forces attacked it, and the grain was lost. Even the accounts of this disagree on where, when, and who led the attack.

text: At first, the Yuan commanders did not even know their supplies were gone.
say: At first, the Yuan commanders did not even know their supplies were gone.

text: They searched for food around Thăng Long, but it kept running short. In March, they pulled back from the capital to their fortified base at Vạn Kiếp, and waited for supplies that did not come.
say: They searched for food around Tahng Long, but it kept running short. In March, they pulled back from the capital to their fortified base at Vahn Kee-ep, and waited for supplies that did not come.

text: At last, Toghan ordered a retreat to China, in two parts: the army overland through the northern mountains, and the fleet by water toward the sea.
say: At last, Toh-gahn ordered a retreat to China, in two parts: the army overland through the northern mountains, and the fleet by water toward the sea.

text: This is the key point. The army did not leave because it lost one battle. It left because, deep in hostile country, it could no longer feed itself.
say: This is the key point. The army did not leave because it lost one battle. It left because, deep in hostile country, it could no longer feed itself.

text: The fleet's route ran down the Bạch Đằng, a tidal river that meets the sea between today's Hải Phòng and Quảng Ninh.
say: The fleet's route ran down the Bahk Dahng, a tidal river that meets the sea between today's High Fong and Kwahng Ninh.

text: Here, the tide shapes everything. Today, the gap between high and low water can reach about three metres, and at low water, the channels between the islands grow narrow and shallow.
say: Here, the tide shapes everything. Today, the gap between high and low water can reach about three metres, and at low water, the channels between the islands grow narrow and shallow.

text: Vietnamese chronicles say this river had trapped invaders before. In 938, Ngô Quyền is said to have planted stakes in the riverbed and destroyed a Southern Han fleet. In 981, the same tradition says, stakes were used again against the Song.
say: Vietnamese chronicles say this river had trapped invaders before. In nine thirty-eight, Ngoh Kwee-en is said to have planted stakes in the riverbed and destroyed a Southern Han fleet. In nine eighty-one, the same tradition says, stakes were used again against the Song.

text: Whether the commanders of 1288 consciously copied those plans, we cannot know. But the chronicles tell these battles as echoes of each other.
say: Whether the commanders of twelve eighty-eight consciously copied those plans, we cannot know. But the chronicles tell these battles as echoes of each other.

text: The Vietnamese commander was Prince Trần Hưng Đạo, still honoured today in temples along this river.
say: The Vietnamese commander was Prince Chun Hung Dow, still honoured today in temples along this river.

text: Before the fleet came, his forces drove large sharpened stakes into the riverbed.
say: Before the fleet came, his forces drove large sharpened stakes into the riverbed.

text: The usual account goes like this. At high water, the stakes were hidden. The fleet was drawn in. As the tide fell, the ships were caught on the stakes, and then attacked.
say: The usual account goes like this. At high water, the stakes were hidden. The fleet was drawn in. As the tide fell, the ships were caught on the stakes, and then attacked.

text: Most historical sources agree on that core. The details are still debated: when exactly the stakes went in, where the fleet was caught, and how stakes this large were set into the riverbed at all.
say: Most historical sources agree on that core. The details are still debated: when exactly the stakes went in, where the fleet was caught, and how stakes this large were set into the riverbed at all.

text: What the sources agree on is the result. The Yuan fleet withdrawing down the Bạch Đằng was trapped and destroyed.
say: What the sources agree on is the result. The Yuan fleet withdrawing down the Bahk Dahng was trapped and destroyed.

text: On land, the retreating army was attacked on its way north through the mountains. Toghan himself barely made it back to China.
say: On land, the retreating army was attacked on its way north through the mountains. Toh-gahn himself barely made it back to China.

text: The third invasion was over.
say: The third invasion was over.

text: For centuries, the battle was known only from written records: Vietnamese chronicles, and the official history of the Yuan, each written by one side.
say: For centuries, the battle was known only from written records: Vietnamese chronicles, and the official history of the Yuan, each written by one side.

text: Even the archaeologists who study the site say detailed knowledge of the battle is limited, because the primary records are few.
say: Even the archaeologists who study the site say detailed knowledge of the battle is limited, because the primary records are few.

text: The stakes are a second kind of evidence. Three major stake yards are known. Yên Giang was reported by local people in 1958. Đồng Vạn Muối turned up while a fishpond was being dug in 1995. Đồng Má Ngựa was found the same way in 2008.
say: The stakes are a second kind of evidence. Three major stake yards are known. Yen Zahng was reported by local people in nineteen fifty-eight. Dong Vahn Mooey turned up while a fishpond was being dug in nineteen ninety-five. Dong Mah Ngoo-ah was found the same way in two thousand eight.

text: Researchers from Vietnam, the United States and Australia mapped the stakes one by one, and cut trenches through the layers of mud.
say: Researchers from Vietnam, the United States and Australia mapped the stakes one by one, and cut trenches through the layers of mud.

text: Wood samples went to laboratories in Vietnam, Japan and New Zealand: some to identify the tree species, others for radiocarbon dating.
say: Wood samples went to laboratories in Vietnam, Japan and New Zealand: some to identify the tree species, others for radiocarbon dating.

text: The species were hard, dense woods. Local legend says the stakes were made of ironwood, and the lab results fit that well.
say: The species were hard, dense woods. Local legend says the stakes were made of ironwood, and the lab results fit that well.

text: The radiocarbon results came back at roughly seven hundred years old, close to the thirteenth century.
say: The radiocarbon results came back at roughly seven hundred years old, close to the thirteenth century.

text: Notice what that does, and does not, prove. Radiocarbon dates when the tree died, within a range of decades. It cannot say who cut the wood, or for which battle.
say: Notice what that does, and does not, prove. Radiocarbon dates when the tree died, within a range of decades. It cannot say who cut the wood, or for which battle.

text: The link to 1288 comes from putting everything together: the dates, the place on an old river channel, the pattern of the stakes, and the written accounts.
say: The link to twelve eighty-eight comes from putting everything together: the dates, the place on an old river channel, the pattern of the stakes, and the written accounts.

text: The mud itself has a story. Under today's fields lies an old riverbed of sand, later covered by clay as the channel silted up. Mangrove pollen shows this was once a tidal estuary.
say: The mud itself has a story. Under today's fields lies an old riverbed of sand, later covered by clay as the channel silted up. Mangrove pollen shows this was once a tidal estuary.

text: The stakes were not one simple fence. They stood in rows, some leaning toward each other, some packed into wall-like lines.
say: The stakes were not one simple fence. They stood in rows, some leaning toward each other, some packed into wall-like lines.

text: Around them, the team found pottery from several centuries, some from the Trần period, a broken oar, and layers of charcoal that suggest fire.
say: Around them, the team found pottery from several centuries, some from the Chun period, a broken oar, and layers of charcoal that suggest fire.

text: Using modern tide levels, the team estimated that at low water this old channel was only about three metres deep.
say: Using modern tide levels, the team estimated that at low water this old channel was only about three metres deep.

text: What is missing matters too. When the team published its results in 2011, no ship remains had been identified. The stakes do not count ships or soldiers, and they do not settle the exact day, or who gave which order.
say: What is missing matters too. When the team published its results in twenty eleven, no ship remains had been identified. The stakes do not count ships or soldiers, and they do not settle the exact day, or who gave which order.

text: Today, the Yên Giang stake yard is kept open to visitors. The others were covered again to protect them.
say: Today, the Yen Zahng stake yard is kept open to visitors. The others were covered again to protect them.

text: Now, the second puzzle. After winning, Đại Việt did not break with the Yuan. It sent envoys and tribute again.
say: Now, the second puzzle. After winning, Dye Vee-et did not break with the Yuan. It sent envoys and tribute again.

text: Victory had a cost. Thăng Long had been ravaged, and in the years right after the war, famine struck the country.
say: Victory had a cost. Tahng Long had been ravaged, and in the years right after the war, famine struck the country.

text: The Trần king wrote to Kublai, describing the destruction the invasions had brought, and still apologised for his "offences".
say: The Chun king wrote to Kublai, describing the destruction the invasions had brought, and still apologised for his "offences".

text: He still would not go to the Yuan court in person. Instead, he sent a golden statue in his place.
say: He still would not go to the Yuan court in person. Instead, he sent a golden statue in his place.

text: For Kublai, the matter was not settled. In 1293 he detained a Vietnamese envoy and was still planning another campaign. When he died early in 1294, the plan was dropped.
say: For Kublai, the matter was not settled. In twelve ninety-three he detained a Vietnamese envoy and was still planning another campaign. When he died early in twelve ninety-four, the plan was dropped.

text: His successor, Temür, declared the war over and restored relations. Tribute continued for the rest of the Yuan dynasty, and no Trần king ever went to the Yuan court.
say: His successor, Teh-moor, declared the war over and restored relations. Tribute continued for the rest of the Yuan dynasty, and no Chun king ever went to the Yuan court.

text: In this world, tribute was a ritual between courts. Sending it did not mean Yuan officials governed Đại Việt. The Trần kept ruling their own kingdom.
say: In this world, tribute was a ritual between courts. Sending it did not mean Yuan officials governed Dye Vee-et. The Chun kept ruling their own kingdom.

text: Yuan sources saw a stubborn vassal. Later Vietnamese histories saw resistance and victory. Both describe the same events, from opposite sides.
say: Yuan sources saw a stubborn vassal. Later Vietnamese histories saw resistance and victory. Both describe the same events, from opposite sides.

text: So the river and the tide won the battle. But keeping the Trần on their own throne took something slower: tribute, letters, and careful refusals, for years after the fighting stopped.
say: So the river and the tide won the battle. But keeping the Chun on their own throne took something slower: tribute, letters, and careful refusals, for years after the fighting stopped.

text: If you know a source we missed, or think we got something wrong, tell us in the comments. Sources are in the description.
say: If you know a source we missed, or think we got something wrong, tell us in the comments. Sources are in the description.
